summary:
I've been building a fleet health dashboard and app launcher that watches four machines and doubles as a jump point to about 29 internal and public apps. The part worth mentioning is a colorblindness bug I caught after shipping: I'm deuteranopic, and the first version used a conventional green/amber/red status palette that, when I actually simulated it, put ok and fail at a color distance of 15.5 — basically indistinguishable. I swapped to blue/amber/crimson (a distance of 98) and locked it in with a test that re-runs the simulation against the live stylesheet, plus a companion test proving the old palette would fail the guard. Status also never rides on color alone anymore — distinct glyphs and printed words back it up.

Running the dashboard's CI turned up its own infrastructure trap: `gitea.dev` looks like an internal-only hostname but is actually a real, publicly registered domain, and only its IPv4 record is overridden to point at my local Gitea. IPv6 still resolves to the public internet. A client that happened to prefer IPv6 would push credentials and repo contents to a server I don't control — it's only safe today because IPv4 wins in practice. Flagged it, not yet fixed.

Separately, I spent a debugging session chasing a systemd hardening setting (`NoNewPrivileges`) that silently broke `crontab -l` for a hardened service — no error, it just came back empty, which looked like "zero cron jobs" instead of "can't read the spool." The fix was adding the unit to the `crontab` and `adm` groups so it can traverse the spool directory and read the journal.

On the LLM-serving side, I benchmarked thread counts and memory-mapping tradeoffs for the local model server that backs a few of these tools, and found the "obvious" tuning move — cranking thread count to match SMT sibling count — actually costs about 31% of generation throughput and triples the variance, versus just leaving it at the physical core count. Small thing, but it's the kind of assumption that's easy to carry over from unrelated benchmarks without re-testing on your own hardware.

highlights.oneLiner: Fixed a colorblind-unsafe status palette in the fleet dashboard, locked in with a CVD simulation test.
Benchmarked llama.cpp thread tuning; matching thread count to SMT siblings cost 31% throughput.
Traced a split-horizon DNS gap in CI where an internal hostname still resolves publicly over IPv6.
